name: Saul
bio: Saul, a young man, was present at Stephen's stoning, where the witnesses laid their garments at his feet (Acts 7:58). His conversion and transformation into the apostle Paul are told in detail in the chapters ahead. Saul approved of Stephen's death and, in the great persecution that followed, ravaged the church, entering homes and dragging off men and women to prison (Acts 8:1-3). Still breathing threats against the church, Saul obtained letters authorizing him to arrest believers in Damascus, but on the road a blinding light from heaven knocked him to the ground, and he heard Jesus's voice asking why he persecuted him. Blind for three days, Saul was found by Ananias, whom the Lord had sent despite his fears, since Saul was a chosen instrument to carry Jesus's name to the Gentiles; Ananias restored his sight, and Saul was baptized and filled with the Holy Spirit. He immediately began preaching Christ in the Damascus synagogues to the astonishment of those who had known him as a persecutor, until a Jewish plot to kill him forced the disciples to lower him from the city wall in a basket. In Jerusalem, the disciples were afraid of him until Barnabas vouched for him before the apostles, after which Saul preached boldly until another plot forced him to flee to Tarsus (Acts 9:1-30). Barnabas found Saul in Tarsus and brought him to Antioch, where they taught together for a year among the growing number of Gentile believers, who were first called Christians there; when the prophet Agabus foretold a famine, Saul and Barnabas were entrusted with carrying relief to the believers in Judea (Acts 11:25-30).
